Need To Know
Gloria Steinem Dies
Feminist activist, journalist, and author Gloria Steinem
died Wednesday
at her home in New York City at age 92, her foundation announced yesterday.
Steinem became one of the most recognizable leaders of the modern women’s movement, spending six decades advocating for gender equality, reproductive rights, and women’s political representation. Her national profile began with a 1963 exposé of working conditions at New York’s Playboy Club, where she spent 11 days undercover as a Bunny (
see photos
). She cofounded Ms. magazine in 1971—read
her reflections
on the first issue. She helped establish the National Women’s Political Caucus and Women’s Media Center and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013. See how the movements she helped lead
reshaped American life
. Her final memoir, “An Unexpected Life,” is due out later this month.
Explore six decades of her
personal archives
and watch a 2008 interview with Steinem reflecting
on her career
A Changing Game
College football
returns
this weekend with a packed slate of games. No. 9 Ole Miss, facing No. 24 Louisville on Sunday (7:30 pm ET, ABC), is the lone ranked matchup, but Week 1 features multiple storied programs clashing (see
full schedule
No. 11 LSU hosting Clemson (7:30 pm ET, ABC) is widely considered Saturday’s marquee game. The Bayou Bengals and new coach Lane Kiffin have drawn scrutiny by attempting to roster players who signed NFL contracts. Those athletes sought another year of college eligibility by
challenging NCAA rules
—a move opposed by the Southeastern Conference, which is reportedly considering suspending or
expelling LSU
in response. Sunday’s lineup includes No. 4 Notre Dame playing Wisconsin at Lambeau Field (7:30 pm ET, NBC).
The action follows a brief Week 0 schedule that saw former New England Patriots coach Bill Belichick lead North Carolina to a
15-10 victory
over TCU in Dublin, Ireland.

Nvidia Stacks Up
Nvidia is
purchasing Hugging Face
—a repository of open-source AI models—for $12.9B, the company announced yesterday. The deal positions the world’s most valuable company to expand its control of the AI ecosystem beyond supplying semiconductor chips.
Hugging Face received a private-market valuation of $4.5B only three years ago. Since then, it has attracted more than 18 million users and 200,000 companies that use the platform to discover, share, and collaborate on more than 3 million open-source AI models (
open- and closed-source models, explained
). By purchasing the world’s biggest open-source AI model repository, Nvidia positions itself for a day when chip demand may slow. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approval.
When Hugging Face was the subject of an OpenAI hack in July, the company closed the vulnerability using a Chinese open-source model. See five of the most fascinating takeaways
from the hack
